keyFindings.description: BLOCKING, and nothing to do with the code: the pull request conflicts with its base. GitHub reports `mergeable: false`, `mergeable_state: dirty`, read twice ten seconds apart so it is a settled computation rather than one in flight. `main` has moved 18 commits ahead of the merge base 61552da1b1b7 since this branch was cut, and among the files it changed are docs/kubernetes.md, deploy/kubernetes/daemon/legion.yaml.example and packages/claude-envoy — all of which this branch also edits heavily. I cannot approve a head that cannot merge, and approving it would be worse than useless: a conflict merge pushed above an approved head brings the base's paths above it, so READY would be refused READY_UNREVIEWED_CHANGE and the work would come back here anyway (skill://legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md). While the pull request is CONFLICTING, GitHub runs no workflow triggered `on: pull_request` for any of its activity, so no later push gets CI until the conflict is cured. The procedure is the implementer's and is in skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md: record the fingerprint at the current tip, forward-merge the base into the issue branch in one new commit (`jj new legion/INFRA-31 "main"@origin`, from the bookmark and never from `@`, never `jj rebase`), resolve in that one commit, push it as a code push with no skip-checks line, and post the `rebase <old> → <new>; fingerprint <before> → <after>` comment. Then I compare the fingerprint at the `commit_id` of my last submitted review with the new head: equal, and because my last review was a request for changes, this round continues against the new head rather than restarting.
